$comment: Owner WhatsApp agent (plan §8 stage 6a). Loaded ONLY by src/lib/owner-agent/runner.ts via `claude -p --settings <this file> --setting-sources project`, the same way the fleet loads its tier files. dontAsk = fail-closed: anything not allowed is denied, there is no TTY to prompt. deny ALWAYS beats allow. ALLOW: the seven OFFERED owner-agent tools by explicit id (registry.ts OWNER_AGENT_TOOLS), not `mcp__owner_agent__*` and not all nine — the two pending-migration tools (billing_summary, rsvp_totals) stay unallowed here even if a future server bug registered them, and moving a tool into OWNER_AGENT_TOOLS fails src/lib/owner-agent/owner-agent-settings.test.ts until this list is edited on purpose. Per run the runner narrows further: the MCP server registers only the tools the caller's permissions unlock, and --allowedTools names exactly those. DENY: every built-in tool family of the installed CLI (2.1.281), although `--tools ""` already removes them all — this list is the wall that still stands if a future edit drops that flag; plus tier0's secret Read denies, verbatim. HOOKS: fleet guard.sh is deliberately NOT wired. It inspects only `tool_input.command`, and an MCP call carries `{range}`, so it would exit 0 on every call this session can make — a wall in name only. disableAllHooks instead guarantees that no settings-file or plugin hook (for example the repo's SessionStart main-inbox.sh) runs on an owner's question. ⚠️ In print mode the CLI SILENTLY IGNORES a settings file that fails validation (its --help), so this file uses only keys seen in tier0 or in the 2.1.281 settings schema; the runner's flags (--tools "", --strict-mcp-config, --allowedTools, dontAsk) and the server-side filter hold even without it.
